extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in differential geometry / geometric analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of long-time behavior of the (normalized) Ricci flow on surfaces and related results (definitions, evolution equations, a priori estimates, Harnack inequality, convergence cases depending on Euler characteristic) plus sphere theorems in dimensions 3 and 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic scalar curvature ratio (A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A = lim sup_{s -> +∞} R s^2, where s is distance to a fixed point O and R is scalar curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition is independent of the choice of O and invariant under dilation; it is a useful geometric invariant especially on manifolds with positive sectional curvature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive sectional curvature implies A > 0 (except low-dimensional exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For complete noncompact n-dimensional (except n = 4 or 8) Riemannian manifolds of positive sectional curvature, the asymptotic scalar curvature ratio A must be > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a collection of results due to Greene–Wu, Eschenburg–Shrader–Strake, Drees, Chen–Zhu, Ni–Tam and relates to gap theorems used in geometric analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton's theorem on steady gradient solitons and A = +∞
rubrics_metrics.description: If (M,g) is a complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton with bounded curvature and positive sectional curvature, of dimension n ≥ 3, and the scalar curvature attains its maximum at a point O, then the asymptotic scalar curvature ratio A = lim sup_{s->∞} R s^2 = +∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses: steady gradient soliton, bounded curvature, positive sectional curvature, scalar curvature maximum at a fixed point. The proof flows along the soliton potential and uses compactness arguments and Shi's estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanding gradient Ricci soliton with positive Ricci curvature is diffeomorphic to R^n
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete expanding gradient Ricci soliton with Rij + ρ g_{ij} = ∇i∇j F for some ρ > 0 and positive Ricci curvature, the potential F is exhausting and convex and the manifold is diffeomorphic to Euclidean space R^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument uses an identity relating F and R (a constant C appears) and the convexity/exhaustion properties of F to deduce the topology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of 2D steady Ricci soliton (cigar)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only complete steady Ricci soliton on a two-dimensional manifold with bounded curvature which attains its maximum at an origin is the cigar soliton on R^2 with metric ds^2 = (dx^2 + dy^2)/(1 + x^2 + y^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses evolution of scalar curvature, maximum/strong maximum principle, conformal/holomorphic vector fields for gradient solitons, convexity of the potential F, and explicit ODE integration to get the metric form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalized Ricci flow on compact manifolds and volume normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The normalized Ricci flow is ∂g_{ij}/∂t = (2/n) r g_{ij} - 2 R_{ij}, where r = (∫_M R dV)/Vol(M) is the average scalar curvature; this normalization preserves the total volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The normalized and unnormalized flows differ by a dilation factor ψ(t) and a reparametrization of time; one can pass between them using scaling relations and choose ψ so that total volume = 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree conversion lemma for evolution equations (Lemma 5.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P satisfies ∂P/∂t = ΔP + Q under the unnormalized Ricci flow and P has degree k (˜P = ψ^k P under scaling), then under the normalized Ricci flow ∂˜P/∂˜t = ˜Δ ˜P + ˜Q + (k ˜r / (2n)) ˜P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a systematic way to convert evolution equations from the unnormalized to the normalized flow; e.g., it explains extra zeroth-order terms proportional to the average scalar curvature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface Ricci curvature relation and normalized flow equation on surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: On a surface Rij = (1/2) R g_{ij}, so the normalized Ricci flow reduces to ∂g_{ij}/∂t = (r - R) g_{ij}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently the evolution of the scalar curvature under the normalized flow is ∂R/∂t = ΔR + R^2 - r R; the sign of scalar curvature (nonnegativity/nonpositivity) is preserved by the flow via the maximum principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of potential φ with mean zero: Δφ = R - r
rubrics_metrics.description: On a compact surface there exists a unique function φ with mean value zero solving Δφ = R - r, where r is the average scalar curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiating in time and using evolution equations gives an evolution equation for φ: ∂φ/∂t = Δφ + r φ + b(t) where b(t) is determined by normalization conditions (integral constraints). This potential is used to analyze decay and convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and evolution of h (energy-like quantity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define h = Δφ + (1/2)|∇φ|^2 + (R - r) (combination forming a convenient scalar) and set M_{ij} = ∇i∇j φ - (1/2) Δφ g_{ij} (traceless Hessian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evolution of h satisfies an equation of the form ∂h/∂t = Δh - 2 |M_{ij}|^2 + r h (Lemma 5.1.2), which yields differential inequalities used to obtain pointwise bounds for R and related quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper and lower scalar curvature inequalities (short-time bounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist constants depending on the initial metric such that R(x,t) ≤ C1 e^{r t} + r and R_min(t) ≥ -C2 for all t > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bounds (equations (5.1.6) and (5.1.7)) follow from the evolution of h and the maximum principle; combining them yields long-time existence of the normalized flow on compact surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-time existence on compact surfaces (Proposition 5.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any initial metric on a compact surface, the normalized Ricci flow exists for all time t ∈ [0, +∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uses curvature bounds from evolution equations and the maximum principle together with standard parabolic theory (and Shi's estimates to control derivatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convergence classification by Euler characteristic (three cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-time behavior of the normalized Ricci flow on a compact surface depends on χ(M): (1) χ(M) < 0 (r<0): flow converges in C^∞ to a metric of negative constant curvature; (2) χ(M) = 0 (r=0): flow converges to a flat metric; (3) χ(M) > 0 (r>0): flow converges to a metric of positive constant curvature (round sphere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each case uses different estimates: exponential convergence to r when r<0; decay estimates (R ≤ C/(1+t)) and potential renormalization when r=0; entropy/Harnack/no-local-collapsing and integral estimates for r>0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decay estimates in the χ(M) = 0 case
rubrics_metrics.description: When r = 0, there exists C3 such that |∇^2 ϕ|^2 + ϕ^2 ≤ C3/(1+t) and consequently R(x,t) ≤ C5/(1+t) for some C5 depending on the initial metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These polynomial-in-time decay estimates are obtained from the heat equation for the renormalized potential and maximum principle arguments (equations (5.1.12)–(5.1.15)). They are used to prove convergence to a flat metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harnack inequality for normalized Ricci flow (Chow Lemma 5.1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a Harnack-type inequality: for any x1,x2 ∈ M and t2>t1≥0, R(x2,t2) - s(t2) ≤ (R(x1,t1) - s(t1)) exp{Δ/4 + C(t2 - t1)}, where Δ is an infimum of energy integrals over paths connecting x1 to x2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inequality (a generalization of Hamilton's Harnack) controls space-time oscillation of curvature and is a key tool for obtaining pointwise curvature bounds and propagation estimates in the χ(M)>0 case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform curvature bounds for χ(M) > 0 (Proposition 5.1.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a compact surface with χ(M) > 0, there exist t0 and C>0 (depending on initial metric) such that for all t ≥ t0 and x ∈ M, 1/C ≤ R(x,t) ≤ C (i.e., scalar curvature is uniformly bounded above and below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof combines the Harnack inequality, volume noncollapsing (Perelman's no local collapsing theorem I′), Laplacian comparison, and diameter control to obtain global upper and lower bounds on R for large t.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume non-collapsing lower bound for geodesic balls
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Perelman's no local collapsing (I′) and finite maximal time facts for corresponding unnormalized flow, one gets a uniform lower bound Vol_t(B_t(x0,1)) ≥ C2 for t large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lower bound on ball volume is used (with Laplacian comparison) to deduce diameter bounds and ultimately uniform curvature bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponential decay of traceless Hessian M_{ij} (Proposition 5.1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a compact surface with χ(M) > 0, there exist c, C > 0 so that |M_{ij}|^2 ≤ C e^{-c t} for t ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the evolution of |M_{ij}|^2 (Lemma 5.1.8 / equation (5.1.23)) and the uniform positive lower bound of R for large time; exponential decay implies convergence (modulo diffeomorphisms) to a shrinking gradient Ricci soliton.

rubrics_metrics.name: No nontrivial shrinking Ricci solitons on compact surfaces (Proposition 5.1.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a compact surface, the only shrinking Ricci solitons are constant-curvature metrics; there are no nontrivial shrinking solitons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the Kazdan–Warner identity applied to the soliton equation ∇_i X_j + ∇_j X_i = (R - r) g_{ij} and integral identities to force R ≡ r.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion: exponential C^∞ convergence on χ(M) > 0 (Theorem 5.1.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For χ(M) > 0, the normalized flow exists for all time and converges in the C^∞ topology to a metric with positive constant curvature (round sphere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination of exponential decay of M_{ij}, nonexistence of nontrivial shrinking solitons on compact surfaces, and compactness theorems yield C^∞ convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical sphere theorems and curvature pinching statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical sphere theorems: (i) If 1/4 < K_M ≤ 1 (sectional curvature pinching) on a complete simply connected n-manifold then M is homeomorphic to S^n; (ii) If there exists δ < 1/4 with δ < K_M ≤ 1 then M is diffeomorphic to S^n (differentiable sphere theorem). Berger's rigidity: with 1/4 ≤ K_M ≤ 1, M is either homeomorphic to S^n or isometric to a symmetric space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These classical curvature-pinching topological/rigidity criteria are recalled as background for Ricci-flow-based differentiable sphere theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton's differentiable sphere theorems via Ricci flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 5.2.1: A compact 3-manifold with positive Ricci curvature is diffeomorphic to S^3 or a quotient thereof. Theorem 5.2.2: A compact 4-manifold with positive curvature operator is diffeomorphic to S^4 or RP^4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These results use Ricci flow to improve pinching: positive curvature is preserved and the metric becomes rounder under the flow; the pinching estimate is a key step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weakly positive curvature classification (Theorem 5.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) A compact 3-manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature is diffeomorphic to S^3 or a quotient of S^3, S^2 × R or R^3 by fixed-point-free isometries. (ii) A compact 4-manifold with nonnegative curvature operator is diffeomorphic to S^4, RP^4, S^2 × S^2 or quotients of R^2 or R^4 by groups of isometries (statement continues in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These classify possible topologies under weak nonnegativity assumptions; Ricci flow and its long-time behavior are used to obtain these structure results.
